Q: Finding the second largest element in array without sorting A: 
# 2nd largest element in an array without sorting and if both are largest print -1
# number is straight taken from arrAnd you can also use range function from [0,len(arr)]

Largest=2_largest=-1
For i in arr:
   If num>largest:
      2_largest=largest
      Largest=number
   Elif number>2_largest and number!= Largest:
      2_largest=number

Q: How to monkey patch Leaflet library? A:

Your monkey-patch is fine. The real problem: in a production build your app and the plugin end up with two different L objects.

Leaflet 1.x is a CommonJS/UMD package (its package.json has only "main", no "module"/"exports"), and that changes how the bundler wires it up:

  • import * as L from "leaflet" compiles to __toESM(require("leaflet")), a new namespace object, copied at import time. That's the b in your b.ellipse is not a function.

  • Your plugin's import line is commented out, so its bare L compiles to the global window.L (set by Leaflet's UMD wrapper). In the built file you can see the plugin emit L.ellipse=function... (global) while your call emits b.ellipse(...) (the copy).

So the plugin adds .ellipse to window.L, but your code reads it off b, which was snapshotted before the patch. Dev works only because Vite serves one shared module object, so there's no copy to fall out of sync. (In the broken build typeof window.L.ellipse === "function": the patch lands, just not where you read it.)

Fix: use the CommonJS default import. For a CJS module the default export is the real module.exports object (the same one window.L points to), not a fresh copy. In map.tsx:

ts

// import * as L from "leaflet";
import L from "leaflet";

That one line makes the built bundle work. Your declare module "leaflet" block is types-only and keeps working.

Recommended (more durable): also give the plugin a real import instead of relying on the UMD global, in src/l.ellipse.js:

js

import L from "leaflet";   // was: // import * as L from "leaflet";

Now the app and the plugin reference the same object regardless of any global, and it won't break if Leaflet ever ships as pure ESM.

I verified both against a fresh npm run build plus a headless load: the TypeError is gone and L.ellipse([...]).addTo(map) runs.

Takeaway: don't expect L.ellipse = ... on an import * as L namespace (or on the global) to be visible to other importers, because that namespace is a copy. Share the underlying object via the default import instead.
